mcp.serenaMigrate.summary: Move a project-scope Serena registration out of this repo's .mcp.json
mcp.serenaMigrate.detail: Asked by install-mcps.sh:328 when this project's .mcp.json already registers 'serena' (written by an earlier bootstrap, carrying a machine-specific absolute --project path). true runs 'claude mcp remove serena -s project' so the entry can be re-added at local scope in ~/.claude.json; false leaves the existing .mcp.json entry in place and working, and the prompt returns on the next run. .mcp.json may be committed team config, which is why the removal is offered rather than forced.

mcp.serena.summary: Register Serena at local scope for this project
mcp.serena.detail: Asked by install-mcps.sh:341 when no Serena registration exists for this project. true runs 'claude mcp add --scope local serena ...' with this project's absolute path, storing the entry in ~/.claude.json under this project's key — per-project, machine-local, never written to the repo's shareable .mcp.json. false leaves the project without Serena; code navigation falls back to Grep/Glob.

mcp.playwrightConflict.summary: How to resolve a committed .mcp.json that already registers its own playwright server
mcp.playwrightConflict.detail: The three-way conflict menu at install-mcps.sh:501, reached only when this project's git-tracked .mcp.json registers 'playwright' (team-owned, so bootstrap never modifies it). 'shared' registers the bootstrap server as 'playwright-shared' and disables the project entry on this machine only via disabledMcpjsonServers in .claude/settings.local.json. 'alongside' registers 'playwright-shared' and leaves the project entry active, so browser tools appear twice. 'skip' changes nothing. This is the prompt that re-asks on every run even after being answered: 'shared' and 'alongside' both leave a registered 'playwright-shared' plus a live project 'playwright', and the gating condition cannot tell those two end states apart — remembering the answer is what fixes it. Values are stored by name, never as the raw menu digits 1/2/3, so the meaning survives a menu reorder.

mcp.playwrightReplace.summary: Replace an existing machine-local Playwright registration with the bootstrap shared server
mcp.playwrightReplace.detail: Asked by install-mcps.sh:522 when a 'playwright' registration exists at local scope, or at project scope in an untracked .mcp.json — machine-local either way, so it is safe to modify with consent. true removes that entry and registers the bootstrap shared server under the canonical name 'playwright'. false keeps the existing entry and registers the bootstrap server alongside it as 'playwright-shared'.

update.legacyDocsAck.summary: Continue 'update' even though a legacy .docs/ directory was detected
update.legacyDocsAck.detail: Asked by update-project.sh:76 when the project still holds .docs/ artifact content from the pre-wiki layout. true continues the update, which scaffolds wiki/ but never touches the .docs/ files. false aborts with exit 0 so the user can run 'npx @codewizard-dt/bootstrap migrate' first. Answering true does not migrate anything — it only stops the warning from blocking every subsequent update.

gitignore.infoExclude.summary: Add .serena/, raw/, and wiki/ to git's local ignore list via .git/info/exclude
gitignore.infoExclude.detail: Asked by merge-gitignore.sh:440 when one or more of .serena/, raw/, wiki/ are not yet excluded. true writes them under the bootstrap sentinel in .git/info/exclude — machine-local, never committed, and unlike .gitignore it does not blind Serena or ripgrep-class walkers; the installed fileSuggestion script restores @-autocomplete for those paths. false leaves git tracking them here; teammates opt in separately by running update themselves. This is INDEPENDENT of the .gitignore section pass governed by gitignore.offerSectionUpdates: declining or disabling sections never disables the info/exclude mechanism, and a pure sentinel repair (all three already excluded elsewhere in the file) runs with no prompt at all regardless of this key. See also prefs.gitTracking, which decides how git treats the preferences file itself — a different question from these three directories.

prefs.gitTracking.summary: How git should treat .claude/bootstrap-prefs.json and bootstrap-prefs.README.md
prefs.gitTracking.detail: New prompt owned by merge-gitignore.sh. Covers both files together: the values file .claude/bootstrap-prefs.json and its generated companion .claude/bootstrap-prefs.README.md. 'gitignore' adds both to the project's .gitignore so the whole team shares that decision. 'exclude' adds both to .git/info/exclude, keeping them untracked on this machine only. 'neither' leaves them visible to git so they can be committed and shared. Unlike the add/skip gates elsewhere in this schema, the declines-only rule does NOT apply here: this is a choice among three outcomes, not a yes/no on adding lines, so the answer is recorded in all three directions and the prompt is genuinely asked once. Related but separate: gitignore.infoExclude covers .serena/, raw/, and wiki/, not these two files.

guides.*.summary: Install a specific optional guide into wiki/guides/
guides.*.detail: One key per entry in sync-wiki-scaffold.sh's OPTIONAL_GUIDES list (sync-wiki-scaffold.sh:88), keyed by the exact entry text including any extension — today that is guides.evals-framework.md and guides.type-checking-templates. true delivers the guide into wiki/guides/ on every run; false keeps it out and suppresses the per-run prompt. A guide already present in wiki/guides/ (or in the legacy .docs/guides/) is refreshed regardless of this key — existing opt-in wins, because the file on disk is the stronger signal than a stored answer. The required guide tier is never gated by these keys.

gitignore.section.*.summary: Permanently decline one titled .gitignore template section
gitignore.section.*.detail: One key per titled section of lib/scripts/templates/gitignore, slugified from the section's banner title: lowercase it, replace every run of non-alphanumeric characters with a single '-', then strip leading and trailing '-' (so 'Node / TypeScript / JavaScript' becomes gitignore.section.node-typescript-javascript). The grammar is deliberately false-only: false remembers a decline and stops that section being offered again. There is intentionally no 'true' value, because a remembered yes would silently append lines to a project's .gitignore on a later run and break merge-gitignore.sh's stated invariant, 'NOTHING is ever added to a project's .gitignore without asking' (merge-gitignore.sh:11). An accepted section is therefore never recorded, so a section that gains new lines in a later template version is still offered by title on the next run rather than appended silently. The one-value grammar is the design, not a typo — do not widen it.

mcp.braveSearch.summary: Install the Brave Search MCP globally for web research
mcp.braveSearch.detail: Prerequisites: a Brave Search API key and a working Docker daemon — the server runs as a shared local container serving HTTP, registered at user scope. true installs and keeps it updated on every run. false means the installer stops offering it: the prompt is never shown again on this machine until the key is changed or removed. The API key itself is never stored in this file or anywhere in the preferences schema.

mcp.context7.summary: Install the Context7 MCP for library documentation lookups
mcp.context7.detail: No prerequisites — no API key and no Docker required. true installs it at the scope chosen by mcp.context7Scope. false means the installer stops offering it: the prompt is never shown again on this machine until the key is changed or removed. Any optional API key prompt is handled outside this schema and is never stored here.

mcp.context7Scope.summary: Registration scope for the Context7 MCP
mcp.context7Scope.detail: Asked by prompt_scope in lib.sh:410 ('Scope for context7 — [u]ser (default) or [p]roject?'). prompt_scope emits exactly two answers, 'user' and 'project' — it has no local-scope branch, and any reply that does not begin with p or P falls through to user. 'user' registers Context7 once for every project on this machine; 'project' writes the registration into the current project's shareable .mcp.json.

mcp.playwright.summary: Install the Playwright MCP for browser automation and UI testing
mcp.playwright.detail: Prerequisite on macOS: a launchd LaunchAgent (com.bootstrap-claude.playwright-mcp) runs the shared HTTP server in the GUI session so headed browsers work; other platforms get a per-session stdio server via npx. true installs it at user scope under the canonical name 'playwright'. false means the installer stops offering it: the fresh-install prompt is never shown again on this machine until the key is changed or removed. This key covers the fresh-install path only — the conflict paths are mcp.playwrightConflict and mcp.playwrightReplace.

obsidian.installApp.summary: Install the Obsidian desktop app via the native package manager
obsidian.installApp.detail: Asked by install-obsidian.sh when the Obsidian desktop app is not yet installed on this machine. true installs it via the native package manager — brew on macOS, flatpak on Linux — and, per the standard sticky-prompt semantics, keeps offering it again on every subsequent run until it is actually present. false means the installer stops offering it: the prompt is never shown again on this machine until the key is changed or removed via /bootstrap-config. The app itself is machine-wide, not tied to any one project, which is why this key is global scope, matching mcp.playwright's scope choice.

obsidian.plugins.summary: Install the bundled Obsidian plugin set (Dataview, Graph Link Types, Breadcrumbs, Front Matter Title, Alias Linker)
obsidian.plugins.detail: Asked by install-obsidian.sh. This is a single bundled prompt covering all five recommended community plugins together rather than one key per plugin. Dataview is a hard prerequisite for Graph Link Types and Breadcrumbs specifically — both read fields that Dataview indexes, so installing them separately would let a user accept one without Dataview and end up with a plugin that silently doesn't work. Front Matter Title has no such dependency (it reads frontmatter directly); it is bundled here purely for prompt-count simplicity, not because it needs Dataview. Alias Linker likewise has no Dataview dependency — it patches Obsidian's core link resolver directly rather than reading Dataview-indexed fields — but it is self-described 'experimental' upstream, and that experimental status is the reason it stays bundled under this same single consent gate rather than being broken out into its own key, consistent with Front Matter Title's 'bundled here purely for prompt-count simplicity' framing above. true installs and refreshes all five plugin folders into .obsidian/plugins/ and enables them in .obsidian/community-plugins.json on every run. false means the installer stops offering the bundle again until the key is changed or removed via /bootstrap-config. Plugin files live inside this project's own .obsidian/ directory, which is why this key is project scope, matching guides.*'s scope choice. Note: Front Matter Title's own per-surface display toggles (Graph, Explorer, etc.) default OFF inside its own settings and are not scripted by this installer — see install-obsidian.sh's printed note for the one-time manual step.

obsidian.graphDefaults.detail: Asked by install-obsidian.sh. true installs .obsidian/graph.json and thereafter keeps it refreshed per template key (search, colorGroups, and the boilerplate display-flag keys) via a sidecar fingerprint file, .obsidian/.graph-defaults-fingerprint.json: a key untouched since the last delivery is silently refreshed to the current template value, a key the user has diverged from gets a one-time interactive prompt asking whether to update it to the new default (a decline is sticky and not re-asked until that key's template value itself changes again), and non-interactive runs never prompt and never record a decline. Force/layout keys (centerStrength, repelStrength, etc.) are never part of the template and are always left untouched regardless of this key. false means the installer stops offering the feature at all until the key is changed or removed via /bootstrap-config. This preference is independent of obsidian.plugins — accepting or declining one has no effect on the other. The file lives inside this project's own .obsidian/ directory, which is why this key is project scope, matching obsidian.plugins's scope choice.

skills.pruneOrphans.summary: Delete stale skill folders in ~/.claude/skills/ left by the wiki rename
skills.pruneOrphans.detail: Asked by install-global.sh:72 when any renamed-away skill folder (the adr-* and prd-* families) is still present in ~/.claude/skills/. true removes those folders with rm -rf; false keeps them, and they continue to appear as duplicate slash commands alongside their renamed replacements. The list of orphan names is fixed in the script — this key does not decide which folders qualify, only whether the deletion runs.

gitCommit.versionBump.summary: How /git-commit handles the version bump before committing
gitCommit.versionBump.detail: 'auto' is today's behavior: the skill picks a bump level and applies it to every version manifest it finds, without confirmation. 'confirm' prints the suggested bump and asks before editing any manifest — 'confirm' IS this key's ask state, so there is deliberately no separate 'ask' value in the grammar. 'never' touches no version file at all. The [patch]/[minor]/[major] commit-subject prefix is written IF AND ONLY IF a version was actually bumped: written under 'auto' and under an approved 'confirm', omitted entirely under 'never' and under a declined 'confirm'. That coupling is the point — release tooling reads the prefix as a claim about what the commit did, so a prefix on a commit that bumped nothing is a false statement the tooling would act on, not a harmless label. This is a choice among three behaviors, not an add/skip gate, so the declines-only rule does not apply — the answer is recorded in all three directions.

gitCommit.autoPush.summary: Whether /git-commit pushes after a successful commit
gitCommit.autoPush.detail: true pushes the current branch after committing; false commits only; 'ask' prompts each time. The default is false because today's behavior is to never push, and defaulting an unanswered key to an outward-facing action that publishes code would break the compatibility guarantee that an absent preferences file changes nothing. The separate rule that /git-commit never creates a branch is unaffected by this key: pushing an existing branch is all that is on offer.

gitCommit.lint.summary: Whether /git-commit runs the /lint fix-cycle before committing
gitCommit.lint.detail: true runs the full /lint workflow (all cycles until clean or issues are skipped) before assessing changes; false (and unset) skip it entirely — this is an opt-in, not an opt-out, so a fresh install never lints without the user having said yes. There is deliberately no 'ask' value: /git-commit never prompts about this per run, it only reads the stored answer.

packageInstall.consent.summary: Whether package-install-consent.js allows package-manager installs for this project
packageInstall.consent.detail: package-install-consent.js is a PreToolUse hook that today denies every package-manager install command (npm install, pip install, uvx --from, etc.) unconditionally. false (and unset, the default) keeps denying exactly as today — no behavior change for a project that has not opted in. 'ask' makes the hook emit permissionDecision: "defer", handing the decision back to Claude Code's own native permission prompt instead of denying outright — this is safe even under headless/bypass runs because Claude Code's own permission system is the one deciding, not this hook blocking. true makes the hook emit permissionDecision: "allow" outright, skipping any prompt at all.

research.persistToRaw.summary: Whether /research writes its report and sources to raw/research/
research.persistToRaw.detail: Governs the Phase 5 file write only. Findings are always synthesized into the response no matter what this key says — false suppresses the on-disk report under raw/research/<slug>/, it does not suppress the research. 'ask' prompts before writing. Note that a per-run override exists even when this is true, so a single invocation can still decline the write; the stored preference and the per-run override are different mechanisms and both must keep working.

research.autoIngest.summary: Whether /research automatically wiki-ingests its saved report
research.autoIngest.detail: Governs what happens right after Phase 5 writes raw/research/<slug>/index.md — it never runs when that write was suppressed (research.persistToRaw=false, a per-run --no-save, or a declined ask), because there is then no raw/ file to ingest. true immediately follows the full lib/skills/wiki-ingest/SKILL.md procedure against the file just written, non-interactively — Step 2's user checkpoint is skipped because the report was just delivered in this same reply, and the skill proceeds straight through the summary page, entity/concept pages, and the index + log entries. false leaves the wiki untouched and keeps suggesting the manual '/wiki-ingest raw/research/<slug>/index.md' command, which is today's behaviour. 'ask' prompts before ingesting this one report and never writes the answer back to the store — a different mechanism from the per-run override on research.persistToRaw, serving the same 'not this one' need at the ingest step instead of the save step.

uatGenerate.promoteTests.summary: Where /uat-generate writes the unit tests it promotes out of UAT cases
uatGenerate.promoteTests.detail: The question is WHERE promoted tests land, not whether they exist. 'dedicated' is today's behavior: they go in the project's dedicated test directory, resolved by looking at the repo first (an existing test directory) and falling back to the language default — test/ for JS/TS, tests/ for Python, spec/ where that is the local idiom. The directory is detected rather than stored, because this grammar is a closed enumeration of literal tokens and a stored path would be free text. 'sibling' puts each test beside the file under test using the language's own convention (src/parse.ts -> src/parse.test.ts). 'never' writes nothing: the skill still runs its promotability analysis and records the verdict on each UAT case, it just creates no file. An existing test file that already covers the unit is extended in place under every value, and a project's visible layout wins over a stored answer that contradicts it — so this key is a default for new work, not an override of the repo. It affects what lands on disk, not how the UAT itself is judged. Legacy true/false/ask values from the key's earlier grammar are mapped by the skill: true -> dedicated, false -> never, ask -> ask once per run.

gitignore.offerSectionUpdates.summary: Master gate for the .gitignore template section review pass
gitignore.offerSectionUpdates.detail: Controls the single opening gate at merge-gitignore.sh:171 ('Review .gitignore updates? (N line(s) across M section(s))'). This is a full three-state key: 'ask' is today's behavior, true runs the section pass without the opening question (each individual section is still offered by title, so nothing is appended silently), and false skips the whole pass with no prompt at all. The key itself never appends a line to any .gitignore — it only decides whether the pass runs. The .git/info/exclude block is OUTSIDE this gate entirely and keeps its own consent prompt: see gitignore.infoExclude. Individual section declines are remembered separately under gitignore.section.*.
